Dana — thank you for the heads-up and the logs, this is top-of-inbox for us. I'm really sorry for the disruption.

Quick notes: we see a correlated rise in 429s from one of our US edge clusters (us-west-2) starting ~08:28 PT and subsequent idle stream disconnects from long-poll chat sessions. Our initial mitigation is to: (1) divert new sessions to a healthier cluster, (2) enable more aggressive prefix KV cache for Novacare routes to reduce tokenization overhead, and (3) temporarily raise per-customer concurrency caps for your account so client retries don't push you into throttles.

I'll loop in our on-call infra lead and our CS manager for the exec sync. ETA for first mitigation changes: ~20 minutes.

— Priyom

Subject: RE: Novacare: Chat connection fallover and client timeouts (5xx/429 spike)

Short tech update (on-call infra):
- Observed behavior: sudden latency increase of 3–4x on Novacare route; tail latencies cause client-side timeouts (~15s) which trigger client retries. Retries are bursting into our rate limiter leading to 429s; some long-running streams then hit idle disconnect guardrails producing 504s on the client.
- Root hypothesis: KV cache miss storm after a cache eviction window aligned with higher-than-usual concurrent sessions. This amplified RPC count to model hosts causing contention and per-route rate limiter tripping.
- Mitigations executed (09:35 PT): divert new traffic to us-east-1 cluster, adjust rate-limiter buckets for Novacare route, bump concurrency cap for their tenant to +40% (temporary).
- Next steps: roll a conservative model-fallback (lower context, quantized variant) for bursty sessions to reduce per-token cost and latency; monitor error rate for 30m.

I'm keeping telemetry open and will send the health link in 5 minutes.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Infra Lead, Redwood Serving Runtime

Dana — quick update from the on-call team: we diverted new sessions to a healthier cluster and bumped the concurrency cap for your tenant; we're also enabling a temporary model-fallback for sessions exhibiting retry behavior. Initial telemetry shows a ~60% reduction in 429 rate for affected routes and queue latency is trending down.

You should see fewer UI freezes and fewer forced reconnects. We will keep these mitigations in place while we watch for a full return to baseline. Jonas will continue monitoring; I'll plan an exec-level 30-minute sync if we don't hit steady state by 12:00 PT.

If you can, please share any recent client SDK versions in use (we've noted a few rapid retry implementations that may be contributing).

Best,
Priyom
